response.justification: Broad, long-tenured engineer with genuine high-throughput distributed systems exposure (micro-services handling millions of HTTP requests/sec at Sociomantic/Dunnhumby), current Staff-level title, and directly relevant hands-on work with AI-agent infrastructure and MCP tooling — which maps well to the AI-native engineering mindset the role treats as baseline. The main gap is the must-have Python: it appears nowhere in the skills list or role descriptions, while TypeScript is a clear strength (inverted from the role's weighting). Evidence of technical strategy ownership, cross-functional stakeholder management, and production on-call/incident response is also thin relative to a Staff IC bar. Worth a screen to probe Python depth, architectural ownership scope, and operational experience before advancing.
strengths: Real high-throughput, low-latency distributed systems experience (millions of req/sec)
Hands-on AI-agent infrastructure and MCP/developer tooling work
Strong TypeScript/Node plus deep craftsmanship practices (TDD, CI/CD, trunk-based)
concerns: No evidence of Python, an explicit must-have
Limited demonstrated technical strategy, scale-level decision-making, or stakeholder management
No stated on-call, monitoring, or incident-response ownership

key_factors.factor: AI-agent tooling and agentic workflow exposure
